title: Integration of screening and identifying ligand\(s) from medicinal plant extracts based on target recognition by using NMR spectroscopy
protocol: Dissolve G-quadruplex d(TTGGGTT)4 in an appropriate buffer solution to achieve a concentration of 0.25 mM.
Remove triethylamine from the dissolved G-quadruplex by dialysis.
For DOSY, mix G-quadruplex d(TTGGGTT)4 and PE with concentrations of 0.25 mM and 3.5 mg/mL, respectively.
Prepare a mixture for relaxation-edited NMR containing PAC and FLJ at concentrations of 8.7×10^-3 mM and 3.5 mg/mL, respectively.
Prepare another sample for relaxation-edited NMR consisting solely of FLJ with a concentration of 3.5 mg/mL.
Place each prepared sample into 5mm NMR tubes with a total volume of 5×10^-4 L per tube.
Insert the NMR tube into the spinner and measure its height accurately with a gauge.
Enter the eject command and wait for 5–10 seconds before pressing the inject button to position the sample in the probe.
Wait for 5–10 minutes for the temperature equilibrium.
Tune and match the probe on the NMR spectrometer.
Lock onto the lock solvent.
Shim the sample using the lock level.
Set the offset value to the HDO resonance for sample-specific settings.
Determine the 90° pulse length at a given power level.
Re-adjust the frequency offset for water signal suppression if necessary.
Use the 1D p3919gp sequence to test whether the extracts contain G-quadruplex ligand(s).
Use DOSY to pick out the peak of the ligand.
Based on the peak of the ligand, use HSQC and HMBC to identify the structure of the ligand.
Adjust the receiver gain per sequence and sample using automatic receiver gain adjustment.
Set spectral width to 20 ppm.
Set number of time domain data points to 32 k.
Set relaxation delay (RD) to 2.0 s.
Set number of scans to 128.
Adjust receiver gain to fill the digitizer closely.
Acquire diffusion-edited spectra using pulse sequence stebpgp1s19.
Set relaxation delay for DOSY acquisition to 2 s.
Set number of scans for DOSY to 128 or higher as required.
Set data points in F2 dimension to 32 k.
Set data points (gradient strengths) in F1 dimension to 32.
Set spectral width for DOSY to 20 ppm.
Set diffusion delay Δ to 0.1 s.
Set gradient length δ to 5.6 ms.
Apply line broadening factor of 0.3 Hz in F2 dimension.
Process raw experimental data using standard 2D DOSY processing protocol in TOPSPIN software version 2.1.
Apply logarithmic scaling in the F1 (diffusion coefficient) dimension.
Acquire <sup>1</sup>H–<sup>13</sup>C HSQC spectrum using sensitivity improvement with echo-anti echo-TPPI.
Apply GARP decoupling of <sup>13</sup>C during acquisition time.
Employ 0.1 μs trim pulses in the INEPT transfer.
Use gradients in back-INEPT.
Set resolution in F2/F1 to 2 k/512 depending on available experiment time.
Set number of scans to 128 depending on experiment time.
Set number of dummy scans to 16.
Set sweep width in F2/F1 to 20 ppm/170 ppm in hsqcetgp.
Set relaxation delay to 2 s.
Use C-H coupling constant of 145 Hz.
Apply Fourier transformation using 1024×1024 points.
Collect <sup>1</sup>H-<sup>13</sup>C phase-sensitive TPPI HMBC spectra.
Apply GARP decoupling of <sup>13</sup>C during acquisition time.
Set resolution in F2/F1 to 2 k/512 depending on available experiment time.
Set number of scans to 128 depending on experiment time.
Set number of dummy scans to 16.
Set sweep width in F2/F1 to 20 ppm/250 ppm in hmbcgplpndqf.
Set relaxation delay to 2 s.
Use long range C-H coupling constant for HMBC at 6.25 Hz.
Apply Fourier transformation using 1024×1024 points.
Use the 1D cpmgpr1d sequence in FLJ without PAC.
Use the 1D cpmgpr1d sequence in FLJ with PAC at different spin-lock times.
Create a difference spectrum using data from presence and absence of PAC to identify changed peaks belonging to ligand.
Utilize HSQC and HMBC spectra based on identified ligand peaks to determine ligand structure.
Adjust receiver gain automatically per sequence and sample.
Process one-dimensional spectra with line broadening set between 0.3–1 Hz unless otherwise specified.

Set parameters for the cpmgpr1d sequence including pre-saturation water suppression, spectral width, number of time domain data points, relaxation delay, number of scans, and receiver gain to optimize signal strength.
Acquire NMR data using the configured cpmgpr1d sequence.
Adjust the water offset for each sample.
Adjust the 90° pulse length for each sample.
Perform automatic receiver gain adjustment.
